project.title: 2D MBL stability is disorder-type dependent: percolation blockade and Diophantine protection
project.hidden_assumption: The stability of 2D MBL can be decided by a single avalanche argument independent of disorder structure.

contradiction.proposition_A: Strong disorder in two dimensions can support an MBL-like stable phase.
contradiction.proposition_B: In two dimensions thermal inclusions trigger avalanches that destroy MBL in the thermodynamic limit.
contradiction.why_not_both: If avalanches always percolate, stable 2D MBL is excluded; if thermalization is blocked or seeds are bounded, the universal avalanche no-go is too strong.
contradiction.resolution: Both claims survive only with boundaries. Quasiperiodic badly approximable potentials have literature-supported strong stability with this project adding Diophantine classification and explicit bounds. Random disorder is not strictly stable in the infinite-time sense but can be operationally stable when many-body thermalization percolation is blocked.

derivation_chain.description: Percolation blockade separates random-disorder operational stability from DRH thermalization.
assumptions: random disorder has finite rare-region probability

derivation_chain.description: Quasiperiodic stability is controlled by finite sojourn length for badly approximable beta.

validation.caveat: Griffiths tail can downgrade strict stability to operational stability

prior_art_search.impact: Core quasiperiodic-MBL stability is prior art; project increment is classification, explicit bounds, and cooperative-avalanche exclusions.

claims.statement: 2D MBL stability is controlled by disorder type and many-body thermalization percolation, not by a single universal avalanche answer.
evidence_for: LP1 knowledge graph records p_block vs p_c as the order parameter
S1-S3 synthesis gives random/quasiperiodic phase distinction
evidence_against: Strict random-disorder stability is not claimed

claims.statement: Badly approximable quasiperiodic potentials support strong MBL stability; the project increment is Diophantine classification and explicit L_max bounds.
evidence_for: S3 synthesis cites multiple prior works and adds L_max <= 2*(M+2)/epsilon
knowledge graph records L_max << xi_perc as support
evidence_against: Core physical conclusion is prior art
2D decomposition is a sufficient condition and can be conservative by about a factor of two

claims.statement: Quasiperiodic 2D MBL is rigorously and unconditionally strictly stable with tau_MBL = infinity.
claims.killed_by: LP1 synthesis downgrade after prior-art and Griffiths-tail audit
evidence_against: WPL Griffiths correction L_eff = L_max + 2*zeta_WPL*log(W/g) may downgrade strict stability
rank>2 and nonseparable potentials require separate audit

claims.statement: Random 2D MBL is strictly stable in the thermodynamic infinite-time sense.
claims.killed_by: LP1 synthesis distinguishes strict stability from operational stability
evidence_against: Random disorder allows rare thermal regions and eventual quantum tunneling
only tau_MBL ~ exp(alpha*L) operational stability survives

predictions.statement: Well-approximable beta should show finite-size drift when system size reaches relevant continued-fraction denominators.
predictions.observable: crossing-point drift in quasiperiodic MBL finite-size scaling
predictions.measurement_conditions: Change beta away from golden ratio toward well-approximable values and compare L near q_n.

predictions.statement: Near p_block = p_c, thermalization fronts should show 2D percolation geometry.
predictions.observable: front fractal dimension and activated dynamics
predictions.measurement_conditions: Random-disorder simulations or cold-atom experiments tuned close to the blockade threshold.

lessons.lesson: Separate literature-established core conclusions from project increments; quasiperiodic stability was not original to this project.
A sufficient-condition 2D reduction must be labeled as conservative and cannot be used as a necessary stability bound.
Use operational stability for random disorder and avoid infinite-time strict-stability wording unless all rare-region and Griffiths channels are closed.
